questions.question: Which process of phase transition is the reverse of deposition?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Sublimation__**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Sublimation is the transition of a substance directly from the solid to the gas phase without passing through the intermediate liquid phase.
 
• Deposition, on the other hand, is the reverse process where a gas transforms directly into a solid without becoming a liquid first.
 
• This makes sublimation the reverse of deposition as it involves a direct solid to gas transition.
 
• Both processes are phase transitions that occur under specific temperature and pressure conditions.

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
 

 Option
 Details
 
 

 1) Sublimation
 Direct transition from solid to gas.
 
 

 2) Fusion
 Melting, or the process where a solid turns into a liquid.
 
 

 3) Solidification
 Freezing, or the process where a liquid turns into a solid.
 
 

 4) Vaporisation
 The phase transition from liquid to gas.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Sedimentary rock** is formed from fragments of other rocks or the remains of plants or animals, which is **option c**.
 
• **Metamorphic rock** is transformed from its original state by high pressure and temperature without melting, which corresponds to **option a**.
 
• **Igneous rock** is derived from magma that was poured out or ejected at the Earth's surface, corresponding to **option b**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sedimentary Rocks:**

 
 
• Sedimentary rocks are typically formed through the deposition of material at the Earth's surface and within bodies of water.
 
• Common processes include weathering, erosion, deposition, and lithification, which transform loose sediment into rock.
 
• Examples include limestone, shale, and sandstone, which often contain fossils and provide critical insights into the Earth's history.
 
 
 
• **Metamorphic Rocks:**
 
 
• Metamorphic rocks are formed under the surface of the Earth through the alteration of pre-existing rocks (igneous, sedimentary, or other metamorphic rocks) by high heat, pressure, and chemically active fluids.
 
• The process, called metamorphism, changes the mineral structure and texture of the rock without melting it.
 
• Examples include gneiss, schist, and marble, which are used in various construction and artistic applications.
 
 
 
• **Igneous Rocks:**
 
 
• Igneous rocks are formed from the solidification of molten magma, which cools either beneath the surface as intrusive rocks or on the surface as extrusive rocks.
 
• These rocks are primarily classified based on their composition and grain size. Common types include granite (intrusive) and basalt (extrusive).
 
• They are often valued for their hardness, durability, and in the case of pumice, for being so lightweight.

questions.question: Which is a reversible, fluorescent red, acidic dye used to stain cytoplasm, red blood cells, collagen and muscle fibres for histological examination?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Eosin__**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Eosin is a fluorescent red dye used extensively in histology.
 
• It stains cytoplasm, collagen, muscle fibers, and red blood cells, providing contrast to hematoxylin's blue-purple staining.
 
• Its application is crucial in the H&E (Hematoxylin and Eosin) staining technique, which is a standard procedure in medical diagnosis.
 
• Eosin works by binding to positively charged proteins in cells, making it an acidophilic dye.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The use of Eosin dates back to the late 19th century, making it a long-established tool in histological studies.
 
• It is not only used in biological staining but also has applications in inks, printing, and sometimes even in cosmetics.
 
• Due to its fluorescent properties, Eosin can also be used in fluorescence microscopy applications.
 
• The staining mechanism of Eosin involves the electrostatic attraction between the dye and the tissue components, leading to differential staining.

• High Yielding Variety (HYV) seeds were a major component of the Green Revolution.
 
• These seeds, developed in Mexico, are credited with significantly increasing food production.

Green Revolution

 
 
 
A period of agricultural transformation in the 1960s and 1970s that increased food production worldwide, especially in developing countries, through the adoption of new technologies, including high-yielding variety seeds, fertilizers, and irrigation methods.

 
 
 

 
 
Norman Borlaug

questions.question: Which concept was proposed by Hutchinson in 1957 to express the relationship of an individual or population to all aspects of its environment?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Ecological niche__**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The concept of the ecological niche was proposed by G. Evelyn Hutchinson in 1957.
 
• It describes how an organism or population responds to the distribution of resources and competitors (i.e., by growing when resources are abundant, and when predators, parasites, and pathogens are scarce).
 
• An ecological niche refers to the role and position a species has in its environment; how it meets its needs for food and shelter, how it survives, and how it reproduces.
 
• Hutchinson's concept of a "niche" includes both the space a species occupies and the functional role it plays within the ecological community.

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
 

 Option
 Details
 
 

 1) Ecological stratification
 Refers to the vertical layering of ecosystems, often used to describe the arrangement of vegetation layers in a forest.
 
 

 2) Ecological pyramid
 Describes the trophic levels in an ecosystem and represents the flow of energy or biomass across these levels.
 
 

 3) Ecological succession
 Is the process by which the structure of a biological community evolves over time, often following a disturbance.

• Tragically, Moseley was killed in World War I, cutting short a brilliant scientific career that had already had a profound impact on chemistry and physics.

questions.question: Which of the following Vedas depicts the life of the early Vedic people of India and has a collection of 1028 hymns divided into 10 mandalas?

• The Rigveda is the oldest known Vedic Sanskrit text and is one of the four sacred canonical texts (śruti) of Hinduism known as the Vedas.
 
• It is composed of 1028 hymns (Suktas) divided into 10 books or mandalas.
 
• The hymns are dedicated to various deities, primarily the Rigvedic deities like Agni (Fire), Indra (the king of gods), and Soma (a sacred potion or plant).
 
• The Rigveda provides insights into the social, religious, and political life of the early Vedic people, making it a crucial source for understanding ancient Indian history and culture.

 3) Yajurveda
 Comprises the liturgy (mantras) needed to perform the sacrifices mentioned in the Vedas, containing both prose and verse forms.

questions.question: The Provincial elections were held for the first time in _______ under the Government of India Act, 1935.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__1937__**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Provincial elections** were held for the first time in **1937** under the Government of India Act, 1935.
 
• This Act introduced provincial autonomy and abolished the system of dyarchy (dual government) in the provinces.
 
• It marked a significant step towards responsible government in India by expanding the electorate and increasing the powers of legislative councils.
 
• The 1937 elections were significant as they were the first to be held under the new system of government, and they resulted in the formation of ministries by the Indian National Congress in several provinces.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
 

 Feature
 Description
 
 
 
 

 **Government of India Act, 1935**
 Was the longest Act of British Parliament ever enacted at that time. It provided a new constitution for India.
 
 

 **Federal Structure**
 The Act proposed a federation of India, combining British India and the princely states. However, this was never implemented.
 
 

 **Reserved and Transferred Subjects**
 Introduced a division of subjects between the Central and Provincial governments into reserved and transferred subjects.
 
 

 **Bicameral Legislatures**
 Established bicameral legislatures in six provinces and introduced direct elections, thereby increasing the participation of Indians in governance.
 
 

 **Advisory Role of British Crown**
 The Viceroy retained control over matters related to defense, external affairs, and communications but acted on the advice of ministers responsible to the legislature on other matters.
